lots.guide_summary: All five entries are US dealer asking prices on 1stdibs (none sold, none unsold at auction). Only one is live (AUD 1,251); four are expired listings marked sold on 1stdibs whose price paid and date are not shown, so they are last asking prices only. All are signed, clean examples. No auction result for a Sylvie was found: I scanned the Invaluable Rene Lalique sold-prices pages back to December 2022 with no Sylvie hits, and WebSearch was unavailable (session budget used). Rate 1.4549 AUD per USD, taken from 1stdibs's own AUD/USD pair on the live listing. Dealer asking prices for clean signed pieces will sit well above what a dirty, unsigned-in-photos example makes at a Tasmanian auction.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence survives, so both maximums are 0. Buyer's premium 19.8% (all-in = hammer x 1.198). Pickup Moonah, freight $0. Current bid: none (0 bids at 30/09/2026).
lots.confidence_reason: Asking evidence only (four of five expired), no auction results, and the Lalique signature is not visible in any photo.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped, but all five were re-dated: the researcher labelled every entry 'live, seen 2026-09-30', yet four pages (id-f_47448342, id-f_8505123, id-f_17547501, id-f_1925122) carry isAvailable false / isSold true and are unlisted. They stay as expired ASKING, not SOLD, because the price paid and date are not shown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Six photos. Photos 1-4 show the classic Sylvie form: two frosted doves breast to breast with clear raised wings; photo 4 shows the clear crystal frog seated in the opening; photo 5 shows the frog on its own. Photo 6 is taken down into the dirty interior (or through the base) and shows debris and staining; enhancing it shows faint curving lines that might be an etched script signature seen through the glass, but nothing is legible. No base or signature view, no paper label seen. Some grime on the wings; wing tips and edges look intact at this resolution but a nibble cannot be ruled out.
lots.condition: Dirty inside with residue and debris; surface grime on wings; no chips clearly seen but edges and wing tips not shown close up; signature unconfirmed.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm and photograph the etched 'Lalique France' signature (usually near the base edge), and check the wing tips, beak points and rim of the flower frog for chips or grinding? Is 'DORE' a typo for 'Doves'?

lots.what_it_is: Walnut two-over-three chest of drawers in early Georgian (George I/II) taste, quartered and cross-banded top, cross-banded drawer fronts, brass bail handles and escutcheons, bracket feet, 92 x 94.5 x 54cm. Gowans itself catalogues it as 'English walnut George III style', i.e. it does not claim period.
lots.guide_summary: No evidence at all: nothing sold, unsold or asking survives because the researcher found none and WebSearch was unavailable to me as well (session budget used). Direct site searches on auction house sites returned nothing usable. Value is unverified.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maximums are 0. Buyer's premium 19.8%. Pickup Moonah, freight $0. No bids at 30/09/2026.
lots.confidence_reason: No market evidence and period versus reproduction is unresolved from the photos.
lots.key_photo_findings: Twelve photos. Quartered, cross-banded top with thumb-moulded edge; veneer lifting and losses at top corners and moulding (photos 5, 6, 12). Drawer side in photo 5 is bright, clean, crisply planed pale pine with little oxidation, which contrasts with the darkened carcase and suggests replacement or later drawer linings (period English walnut chests usually have oak linings with dark oxidised surfaces); dovetails not shown. Back (photos 7, 8) is vertical softwood boards, aged, with gaps covered by dark green tape; small paper label illegible. Sides are plain solid timber with good colour. Bracket feet look old but worn. Gowans' own 'George III style' wording and the fresh drawer linings lean towards a later reproduction or heavily restored piece.
lots.condition: Veneer lifting and losses to top edge and corners, taped back boards, general wear and rubs; drawer linings look later or replaced.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please photograph a drawer's front and rear dovetails and the drawer bottom underside, and the underside of the carcase and feet. Do you consider it period or a later reproduction? What is the paper label on the back?

lots.key_photo_findings: Base mark read at full resolution: incised script 'R.M.' above 'John Campbell', '1935', 'Tasmania' through a yellow-olive glaze, with sandy unglazed foot ring. lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm there are no chips or hairlines to the rim and foot, and whether the raised spot on the body is a firing flaw or damage?
